title: Plaice with pointed cabbage, potato and dill salad

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is whole food or a plain staple: potatoes, cabbage, radishes, yoghurt, wholegrain mustard, plaice, flour and butter.

supermarket.reason: Plaice fillets, pointed cabbage, radishes and Greek yoghurt are all everyday items at Tesco and similar supermarkets.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a pan, a frying pan and a bowl, and the techniques are boiling, shredding and pan-frying.

works.reason: The quantities suit four, the potato and fish timings are right for thin plaice fillets, and frying in two batches is something any cook would work out.

honest_times.reason: 25 minutes of active work covers halving, shredding, slicing, dressing and frying the fish, and the 15-minute cook matches the potato boil.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the lemon, dill and pepper, is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: A raw pointed cabbage and new potato salad with pan-fried plaice suits a July evening, and the cabbage forms the bulk of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English.

hearty_healthy.reason: Fish, potatoes and plenty of fresh vegetables make a proper, balanced family dinner.
